newsitem.title: UK: UK store chief tells fat cat execs 'keep pay fair'.
newsitem.headline: UK store chief tells fat cat execs 'keep pay fair'.

text.p: The chairman of Britain's leading department store chain John Lewis Partnership on Wednesday urged industry leaders to motivate their workforces by reducing the gap in earnings between so-called fat cats executives and employees.

Stuart Hampson, speaking at the Institute of Directors annual convention, said, "I firmly believe we need to find a greater sense of fairness in the relationship between rewards at the top and those throughout the business as a whole."

Hampson said management should not feel guilty about defending proper differentials, but it was not right that management in most businesses reaped a disproportionate share of a company's success through bonuses and share options.
"I don't see the real problem as fat cats. What's wrong is that there are too many thin cats in business who deserve to be fattened up."

He said the Greenbury report into top executives pay had not resolved the problem, but had just led to repackaging. "The 1 million a year club continues to recruit new members as long term incentive plans trip in."

He called for profit sharing at a broad level within companies to provide incentives for staff. John Lewis, which is run as a partnership by its 36,000 staff, pays out a partnership bonus each year, linked to the firm's performance.
Hampson, who last year earned 343,499 pounds ($560,000), received the same 20 percent bonus this year as the rest of his staff.
